println, misconceptions: 6 edges offered

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:println->PrintWithoutFinalNewline | wrong rule: Ends the output with print and expects it to appear right away. | right rule: Finish a line of print calls with println; some systems hold print output until a newline is printed. | | mis:println->IdentifierCaseInsensitive | wrong rule: System.out.Println and System.out.println name the same method. | right rule: Java is case-sensitive: names of variables, methods and classes that differ only in capitalization are different names. | | mis:println->ParenthesesOnlyIfArgument | wrong rule: println with nothing to print can be written System.out.println; without the parentheses. | right rule: A method call always needs parentheses, so an empty line is printed with System.out.println();. | | mis:println->PrintEqualsPrintln | wrong rule: print and println do the same thing, so print(s1); print(s2); puts s1 and s2 on separate lines. | right rule: println ends the line after printing and print does not, so print(s1); print(s2); puts s1 and s2 on the same line. | | mis:println->PrintNewLineFirst | wrong rule: println(s) prints a newline and then s. | right rule: println(s) prints s and then the newline. | | mis:println->PrintedTextIsExecuted | wrong rule: System.out.println("x is 5"); sets x to 5 (text inside the quotes is run as code). | right rule: Characters inside double quotes are printed literally; println only displays them and changes no variable. Only an assignment such as x = 5; sets x. |

if_statement, misconceptions: 22 edges offered

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:if_statement->BracelessMultiStatementBody | wrong rule: Indenting several statements under an if or for makes them all part of its body, even without braces. | right rule: Without braces only the first statement belongs to the if/for; the rest run once, after it. | | err:if_statement->CurlyIfCondition | wrong rule: Writes the if condition inside { } instead of ( ). | right rule: The condition of an if is written in parentheses. | | err:if_statement->SemicolonAfterIfHeader | wrong rule: if (x > 0); System.out.println("positive"); prints only for positive x. | right rule: The ; ends the if with an empty statement, so the next line always runs. | | mis:if_statement->AssignCompares | wrong rule: = compares two values instead of assigning | right rule: x = y copies the value of y into x; x == y is what compares them. | | mis:if_statement->BranchChosenByIntent | wrong rule: Which branch runs is decided by what the programmer meant or by code outside the if, not by whether the condition is true. | right rule: The then branch runs exactly when the condition evaluates to true at the moment it is tested; otherwise the else branch (if any) runs. | | mis:if_statement->CodeAfterIfSkipped | wrong rule: When the then branch runs, the code after the if is skipped. | right rule: After the if finishes, execution continues with the next statement either way. | | mis:if_statement->FalseConditionEndsProgram | wrong rule: A false condition with no else ends the program. | right rule: When an if condition is false and there is no else, execution continues with the statement after the if. | | mis:if_statement->FalseConditionRestartsProgram | wrong rule: When an if condition is false (and there is no else), control jumps back to the start of the program. | right rule: A false condition skips the then branch and execution continues with the statement after the if statement. | | mis:if_statement->IfConditionCheckedInHindsight | wrong rule: Whether the branch runs is decided by the condition after the branch, or from the point inside the body where the condition becomes true. | right rule: The condition is tested once, before the branch;
